title: Harden the CPU worker agent reconnect, lease and shutdown behavior
goal: Inspect the existing worker client and tests. Improve real gaps in retry/backoff, overlapping polls, lease renewal, configuration validation and graceful shutdown so a long-running CPU worker recovers from transient control-plane failures without claiming work it cannot do.
acceptanceCriteria: Configuration errors are reported clearly before the worker claims jobs.
Transient HTTP/network errors use bounded backoff and do not start overlapping polls.
Shutdown stops new claims and uses existing safe release/checkpoint behavior where supported.
Tests cover changed behavior; existing worker-agent tests remain meaningful.

title: Make runtime readiness and worker failures observable
goal: Improve the existing observability/runtime-coordinator path so worker readiness, stale heartbeats, coordinator failures and recovery outcomes can be inspected without fake online states. Make one contained change with tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Reported states come from observed values rather than constants.
New readiness/failure conditions have focused tests.
Secrets and credentials never appear in diagnostics.
Existing coordinator and production-infrastructure tests pass.

title: Expose accurate coordinator readiness in health reporting
goal: Inspect the health route and dashboard tests. Ensure health reporting distinguishes the HTTP server being alive from worker execution being ready. Do not redesign the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: HTTP liveness stays available when no model provider is configured.
Readiness reports actual coordinator and runtime configuration without secrets.
The route never reports execution ready merely because the web process is alive.
Tests cover configured and unconfigured states.

title: Improve build-step failure recovery and actionable diagnostics
goal: Review the existing app/web execution engine, worker checkpoints and executor tests. Make one contained improvement so failed or timed-out build steps are recorded with redacted diagnostics and can be safely retried or blocked without falsely claiming completion.
acceptanceCriteria: A failed or timed-out step never satisfies successful acceptance criteria.
Recovery is bounded and does not duplicate a claimed step.
Diagnostics exclude tokens, passwords, secret values and environment dumps.
Tests cover the changed failure/recovery behavior.

title: Tighten game execution result and verification evidence
goal: Inspect the existing Konami/game executor and verification contract. Prevent missing engine/build/playtest adapters or incomplete outputs from being reported as successful completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing engine-specific runtime support is reported unavailable, not successful.
Verification relies on recorded execution evidence.
Failure reasons are actionable and sanitized.
Existing game executor and verification tests pass.

title: Improve model rate-limit recovery without paid fallback
goal: Inspect model orchestration and model-node execution to improve how HTTP 429/provider transient errors are recorded and delayed. Do not change provider keys, model IDs, budget arithmetic or the model-provider registry.
acceptanceCriteria: Rate-limit failures are identifiable and not retried in a tight loop.
Retry/backoff stays inside configured attempt limits.
Provider errors do not leak keys or response bodies.
Tests cover retryable and non-retryable provider errors.
